overrides/sandworm.body:
# Sandworm (Shah Neshen, the Devourer)

A 20-player Elite Trial in Brimstone Sands. It's one long fight with a big role split. This page follows the fight in the order it happens.

Related: [[1 Raids]] · [[Consumables]] · [[Heart Runes]] · [[Drop Limits]] · [[Gear Basics]] · [[Trophies]] · [[Status Effects]]

## Getting in

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Players | 20 (opens with 12). Fill all 20 slots for enough damage and survivability |
| Level / GS | 65, and groups usually want 690+ (the game suggests 600–625) |
| Entrance | Brimstone Sands, at the arena near the Wormsign Obelisk Shrine, or Activities tab → Elite Trial. You don't need to be near the arena to join |
| Quest | Pick up the repeatable quest from Phaedra Kanelos by the shrine before entering |
| Voice | The whole raid should be in one voice channel |
| Enemy type | Shah Neshen is a Beast: 70% physical and elemental mitigation, and a small (+1%) Thrust weakness. The adds are a mix of Beasts and Angry Earth |
| Debuff caps | Rend: the worm has 50% Rend resilience, so the raid needs 140% Rend to hit the cap. Weaken: 200% (a stated cap) |
| Reviving | Each player can be revived only once per raid. A second death sends you back to the starting platform until the boss dies or the raid wipes. There is a short AFK timer, so keep moving |
| Loot | Daily box once per daily reset and weekly box once per week (from `LootLimits`: Trial_Sandworm_DailyBox / WeeklyBox) |

## Preparation

| Item | Who | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Major Wildlife Combat Trophy** · **Major Angry Earth Combat Trophy** | Everyone | Trophies add damage: Minor +3%, Basic +4%, Major +5%. One of each in each of your three houses gives +15% against Beasts and Angry Earth |
| **Infused Angry Earth Ward Potion** | Melee | 10% less damage from Angry Earth |
| **Infused Beast Ward Potion** | Ranged | 10% less damage from Beasts |
| **Infused Beast Coating** | Everyone | +15% damage against Beasts |
| **Powerful Honing Stone** | Everyone | +7% weapon damage |
| **Powerful Incense** | Everyone | +50 to all afflictions |
| Attribute food | Everyone | Food for your build's attributes |
| **Acid Tincture** | Everyone | Cleanses Acid Burn |
| Health potion | Everyone | |
| Stalwart Heartrune of Fire Storm | Raid | The raid's acid cleanser. Using it to cleanse the players around you is called a "kick" |
| Pickaxe, GS 600+ | Miners | Each mine then takes two hits |

> [!tip] Use your consumables before stepping down into the arena: crossing the door puts you in combat. You can still step back inside to respec or change gear.

## Suggested group

Four groups of five.

| Group 1 | Group 2 | Group 3 | Group 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranged Tank | Offtank | Damage Dealer | Damage Dealer |
| Lights | Lights | Damage Dealer | Damage Dealer |
| Rendbot | Mage | Damage Dealer | Damage Dealer |
| VG / LS | Flail | Damage Dealer | Damage Dealer |
| Butcher / Spear | SnS / Venom | Damage Dealer | VG / LS |

> [!info] There's no single right comp. What matters is that the group reaches the Rend, Weaken and Empower caps and covers the roles below.

## Roles

| Role | Job |
|---|---|
| Shot caller | Calls the light colours, blocks and mechanics (see Shotcalling) |
| Ranged Tank | Holds aggro from range. **Musket** or Bow is common, with **Rapier** as the second weapon for riposting Acid Spits and taunting if needed. **Hatchet** is also good for survivability. The tank can be one of the lights |
| Lights | Three or four players. They press their platform for the lights mechanic, shoot Acid Balls and clear adds. Fewer lights means more melee damage; 4 lights plus a tank who stays on the boss also works |
| Offtank | Makes the scorpion phase faster and safer. Two Nephilim spawn together: the offtank takes one and keeps it busy around the arena until the phase ends, then the raid breaks it and picks up its sword for Storm Chaser |
| Healers | At least one healer. Best is a Void Gauntlet main using Void Blade (melee, adding Rend stacks) with **Oblivion** under the group for Empower. Always bring a second Void Gauntlet / Life Staff healer; a Flail with Life Staff doesn't count as a second healer. More than two isn't needed |
| Mage | Handles mages and ranged enemies with the lights |
| Flail and SnS | Extend everyone's debuffs and damage over time, so DoTs and Rend only need applying once per phase |
| Rendbot | Applies Rend with the War Hammer, then swaps to Rapier |
| Damage dealers | Mostly Rapiers. The worm is stationary, has a back and takes +1% Thrust, so Rapiers shine. Typical comps run 8–13 Evade Rapiers to keep bleeds rolling, plus 2 or 3 Bleed Rapiers to pop them |

> [!info] Advanced groups can use a melee tank instead. A ranged tank holds aggro but can't reliably chain taunts, so a melee tank, or one on each side of the stack rotating taunts, lets the raid benefit from the extra damage that Carnelians on armour give against taunted foes.

### Reaching the caps

**Rend: 140% for the worm, 70% for each scorpion when you split.** Examples:

| Source | Rend |
|---|---|
| Hatchet: **Rending Throw** | 20% |
| War Hammer: **Armor Breaker**, plus Sundering perks for **Clear Out** and **Shockwave** | About 65% together |
| Void Gauntlet: Disintegrate | 30% |

**Empower: aim for the 50% cap.** Prioritise sources that buff the Rapier players.

| Source | Empower |
|---|---|
| **Powerful Honing Stone** | 7% |
| **Oblivion** (Void Gauntlet) | 15% |
| **Omnidirectional Evade** (gear) | Empower on evade |
| Flail: **Leader of the Pack** | 10% to the nearby raid |
| Flail: **Arcane Vortex** | 10%, with almost 100% uptime |
| Sword and Shield: **Leadership** | 10% to the group only |

**Extending debuffs.** The core of the comp is DoTs plus Rend with duration extension, so you apply once per phase and keep extending.

| Source | Extension |
|---|---|
| Flail: **Vital Embrace** | +7% DoT duration |
| Flail: **Arcane Eruption** (Debilitating Extension) | +30% duration to all status effects, Rend included |
| Sword and Shield: **One with the Shield** | +5% debuff duration |
| **Distained Infliction** (perk) | +5% DoT per player |

**Stacking DoTs.**
- The same status effect from the same source doesn't stack beyond its limit. If several of the same debuff are applied, the highest counts.
- Runeglass comes in 6 elements: try to have one of each across the raid.
- Different heartrunes apply different DoTs. Bile Bomb variants are different DoT types, so they stack. Normal and Stalwart Fire Storm also differ and can stack.
- Skewer and Poison Shot apply different DoTs in their upgraded and base versions. Two Skewers from the same tree make 1 bleed; from different trees, 2 bleeds. Perforate's upgraded and base versions apply different Rend stacks.
- Powder Burn needs a headshot, and the worm has no head hitbox, so ignore it here.
- Attunements are extra on-hit damage with about a 1.5 s cooldown, and they don't stack from several sources. Use one of each across different players.

> [!tip] For Rapiers, Keen Awareness beats Thrust Damage. Bleeds are the Rapier's main damage and Thrust Damage doesn't affect DoTs, and Thrust Damage counts towards Empower, which a 20-player raid caps anyway. More crits mean faster cooldowns, more Flurry hits and more bleeds popped.

## How the fight runs

The fight is three phases with a scorpion phase after each, then a final phase that repeats until the worm dies.

| Part | What's new |
|---|---|
| Phase 1 | Acid Balls, spits, Acid Trail, melee attacks; Nephilim and adds |
| Scorpion phase | Two giant scorpions, then the worm's stamina break |
| Phase 2 | Heavy attacks join the rotation |
| Scorpion phase | Same as the first |
| Phase 3 | Mines join the rotation |
| Scorpion phase | Same as the first |
| Final phase | Phase 3 again, alternating with scorpion phases until a clear or a wipe |

**Rotation rules.**
- Its attacks are Acid Balls, Acid Trail, the melee attack, triple and single Acid Spits, heavy attacks and mines.
- A single Acid Spit doesn't count as a full attack.
- Once heavy attacks are in, every rotation has exactly one guaranteed heavy between Acid Balls.
- Each phase does Acid Balls three times, and spawns enemies (Nephilim and adds) after the first and the third.
- Every phase ends with a full rotation, or is forced when the boss loses 30% of its health.
- The worm sometimes goes off script. Single spits shift the rotation, and an Acid Trail almost always comes just before the next big pattern.

## 1. Summoning the worm

Three players interact with the big drum in the centre to summon Shah Neshen the Devourer. DPS stack on the left of the spawn.

The worm is mostly stationary in the centre of the arena. Melee attack its midsection, the ranged tank holds aggro from a distance, and ranged DPS stay on the upper platform to handle mechanics.

### Its attacks

| Attack | What happens | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Acid Balls | The worm looks up and launches acid projectiles into the air. If they land they deal heavy area damage and leave acid circles | At least one player shoots them in mid-air. A **Musket** does this easily: timed well, one shot passes through all of them (Shooter's Stance, or Quick Load with Tactical Reload), and each counts as a kill, which refreshes the ability at once. A Bow works with Penetrating Rapid Shot and Refreshing Penetrating Shot, but only if the Bow player is the only one shooting the Acid Balls; others just clean up strays |
| Acid Trail | A red marker appears over the player with aggro, with a preview of the trail from the boss to them. The worm spews acid along it, and the trail lingers for a few seconds | Slow and easy to avoid: get out of the line |
| Acid Spits | Acid spat in three directions centred on the tank, usually three times in a row but sometimes once. Heavy damage, and it raises acid infliction | Dodge them. Never stand in front of the spit |
| Melee attack (bite) | Two bites in a row, one on each side. Each deals massive damage (an instant kill) and leaves an acid puddle behind | Block with a full stamina bar when the caller says "Block!", or dodge. Then cleanse the acid from the puddle under you |
| Heavy attack (slam) | From Phase 2. The worm slams its body down in a wide sweeping arc | Players on the upper platform are safe, and so are players fighting close to the body. Watch the animation and dodge in time |

> [!warning] Not blocking the melee attack when the caller says "Block!" kills you.

## 2. Phase 1

| Step | What the worm does | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spawn animation | No enemies |
| 2 | Acid Balls | |
| 3 | Attack | |
| 4 | Spawns enemies | Nephilim and adds |
| 5 | 2 attacks | |
| 6 | Acid Balls | |
| 7 | 3–4 attacks | |
| 8 | Acid Balls | |
| 9 | 2–3 attacks | Enough damage can force the phase to end here |
| 10 | Spawns enemies | |
| 11 | 1–2 attacks | |
| 12 | Phases out | Acid covers the upper platform |

### Nephilim and the lights

Each enemy spawn brings Nephilim, large enemies with a stamina shield, plus scorpions, mages and Angry Earth adds. The tank groups the adds, and the lights and mage kill the mages and ranged enemies first.

| Step | What happens | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Lights | Four players stand on the platforms. Each platform hides a colour, red or blue, that the player on it can't see | The shot caller calls the colour for each platform. A wrong press makes that platform lethal for 3 seconds. All four right gives the raid Shield Breaker: bonus shield stamina damage, so the raid can break a Nephilim's stamina with heavy attacks and kill it |
| The sword | A Nephilim drops a huge sword when it dies | Pick it up for Storm Chaser: Siege damage resistance and Rend stacks on the worm. It has limited charges and disappears after a few seconds. Only one player can use it at a time, so don't spam it |

> [!tip] With the right settings you can read your own light without a caller. Settings > Game > Tilt-based Camera Zoom > Enable. Settings > Video > Field of View (FOV) > Max (70).

## 3. Scorpion phase

When the worm finishes its attack rotation, or each time it loses 30% of its health, it dives underground into its cave. The upper platform fills with lethal acid smoke, and one giant scorpion spawns on each side.

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1 | Scorpions spawn on each side |
| 2 | The scorpions leave their caves |
| 3 | The worm chomps up from the ground every 4–5 s |
| 4 | The scorpions die |
| 5 | Sand bursts from the ground four times |
| 6 | The acid on the upper platform weakens |
| 7 | The worm pops up with a stamina bar |
| 8 | The lower arena fills with acid |
| 9 | The stamina breaks, and all the acid disappears |

**Killing the scorpions.** Either split into two groups, one per scorpion, or have one player kite a scorpion while the raid kills the other and then comes to help. While the scorpions are alive the worm attacks from underground: a green circle appears on the ground and the worm lunges up from it, leaving a circle that causes Acid Burn. Stay off the glowing circles and avoid acid pools. Keep the middle clear of acid circles so you can stack there for the stamina break; faster scorpion kills help.

When both scorpions are dead, the tank, a healer, one DPS and two lights take the right stairs; everyone else goes left.

### Stamina break

The worm comes back with a stamina bar. The lights mechanic returns, and players use heavy attacks to break the stamina. The tank holds the worm. A sweep kills anyone slow on the stairs, and the worm spits acid when it faces you, so dodge.

| Approach | How it works |
|---|---|
| Ranged | Everyone goes to the top of the arena and uses ranged weapons to break the stamina. You will get Acid Burn: cleanse it with an **Acid Tincture** or the Stalwart Heartrune of Fire Storm |
| Melee | Only the lights go to the top. Everyone else stacks together in one spot (middle, right or left) and spams heavy attacks; melee weapons do more stamina damage, so it's faster. Downstairs is covered in lethal acid that keeps reapplying, so stand in the heals and chain the Stalwart Heartrune of Fire Storm across players while the caller times the kicks. Riskier, but a lot faster |

> [!warning] In the ranged approach, getting hit by an Acid Spit while you have Acid Burn is an instant kill. Cleanse it straight away.

## 4. Phase 2

Heavy attacks join the rotation.

| Step | What the worm does | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Heavy attack | Unless the boss was broken again after the stamina phase |
| 2 | Acid Balls | |
| 3 | 2–4 attacks | 1 guaranteed heavy |
| 4 | Spawns enemies | |
| 5 | Finishes its remaining attacks | If it did fewer than 5 before the spawn |
| 6 | Acid Balls | |
| 7 | 3–5 attacks | 1 guaranteed heavy |
| 8 | Acid Balls | |
| 9 | 2–3 attacks | Enough damage can force the phase to end here |
| 10 | Spawns enemies | |
| 11 | 1–2 attacks | |
| 12 | Phases out | |

Then a second scorpion phase, the same as the first.

## 5. Phase 3: mines

Exploding mines join the rotation. Mine them quickly before they go off; a mine that goes off deals heavy raid-wide damage and stuns.

| Step | What the worm does | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mines | Unless the boss was broken again after the stamina phase |
| 2 | Heavy attack | |
| 3 | Acid Balls | |
| 4 | 1–2 attacks | |
| 5 | Spawns enemies | |
| 6 | 2–3 attacks | 1 guaranteed heavy |
| 7 | Acid Balls | |
| 8 | Mines | |
| 9 | 2–4 attacks | 1 guaranteed heavy, before or after the mines |
| 10 | Acid Balls | |
| 11 | 0–1 attack | Enough damage can force the phase to end here |
| 12 | Mines | |
| 13 | Spawns enemies | |
| 14 | 1–2 attacks | |
| 15 | Phases out | |

**Mining.** You don't need the whole raid to mine. Assign a group, or specific players, to the mines in the arena; the lights take care of the mines on top. Watch for the heavy attack while mining.

> [!warning] In Phase 3 there's always a heavy attack before or after the second wave of mines. If the worm throws mines without a heavy in that stretch, the heavy comes straight after, so call it out. The safer way is to send the miners after the heavy.

Then a third scorpion phase, the same as the first.

## 6. Final phase

Phase 3 repeats, alternating with scorpion phases, until the worm dies or the raid wipes.

## Shotcalling

### Blocks

The melee attack has a unique sound cue you only hear when it happens: memorise it, as it's the fastest and most consistent way to call blocks. Use one word, "Block!", every time: players with voice delay or slow reactions can die waiting for a longer call. You can also watch the attack: the first hit is on a random side, so if it's on the other side, call "Block the second" to save a few seconds of damage.

### Calling lights

You don't need to count every attack: watch for the Acid Balls. Each phase spawns enemies after the 1st and 3rd Acid Balls, and enough damage phases the boss before the second spawn, so ideally you call lights once per phase.

| Phase | When to call lights |
|---|---|
| Phase 1 | Enemies spawn after 1 attack rotation (after 2 about 10% of the time). Call lights as soon as the first attack is done |
| Phase 2 | Enemies spawn after 2–4 attacks. There's always a heavy attack, directly before or after the spawn about 95% of the time. Call lights as soon as it does a heavy or starts spawning Nephilim |
| Phase 3 | Enemies usually spawn after 2 attacks, and very likely straight after an Acid Trail. Call lights after the 1st attack: whether it spawns or does one more attack, there's enough time |
| Second call | If damage is low and around 80% of the bar is still needed to phase, do a second round after the 3rd Acid Balls: call lights right after the second attack that follows them |

Call during the attack, not after it ("lights after the last spit", "lights after the lick"), so the lights get into position early. On rare occasions the worm does two single spits, which count as an attack. Give the "look up" call for Acid Balls even when it isn't needed; it helps you memorise the patterns. Keep in touch with your offtank: if their Nephilim is broken early, the lights mechanic has to be done again.

### Calls

| Call | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Dodge | Roll to avoid a worm attack or knockback, usually when it pops out of the ground in the scorpion phase or before the stamina phase |
| Look up | For the lights: shoot the Acid Balls |
| Lights | Lights players press their platforms |
| Block / Block the second | Block the melee attack with a full stamina bar |
| Kill the Nephilim | Heavy attacks to break its stamina and kill it |
| Pick up the sword | Grab the Nephilim's sword for more Rend on the boss |
| Mages | The spawned enemies are mages (or melee), so the mage and lights deal with them |
| Lights up, everybody down | Melee stamina: lights back to their platforms, everyone else clumps together |
| Everyone go up | Ranged stamina: everyone upstairs after the scorpions die |
| Kicks | Use the Stalwart Heartrune of Fire Storm to cleanse the players around you |
| Go mining | The mining group splits up in the bottom area to mine the ores |
| Heavy attack, prepare to dodge/block | Warning for players far from the worm, usually the miners |

### Managing the raid

- If a lights player goes down, call another lights player to revive them; don't assume they'll notice. If they're fully dead, send someone else up to press the lights, so know your backup lights in advance.
- The Flail and SnS keep extending the debuffs. If they die, call the support players, mainly the rend players, to keep reapplying Rend, since it's no longer extended.
- Call out whether spawned enemies are mages, ranged scorpions or melee, so the lights and mage can deal with them.
- Before the raid starts, say who cleanses (kicks), who mines, and which side each player takes in the scorpion phase.

### Wipe or keep going?

- If your main rend players die halfway through, reset: finishing takes longer than restarting, and you're more likely to wipe.
- With 3–5 damage dealers dead you can still finish if the rest are experienced. Make sure there are enough kicks left for a melee stamina phase.
- Melee stamina relies more on players than ranged. Start learner and practice raids with ranged stamina: you can still finish with 10 players dead, while losing 5–6 in melee almost always means a wipe.

## Debuffs and buffs from the game data

| Name | Effect |
|---|---|
| Acid Pool | 4% max health as Acid every 0.5 s, plus Acid affliction. Get out, or use an Acid tincture |
| Acid Storm | 1.5% max health as Acid every second |
| Digestive Juices | 2.5% max health as Acid every 0.5 s (where it devoured) |
| Acid Spew | 25% max health as Acid every second. Never stand in front of the spit |
| Poisoned (scorpions) | 4% base + 2% base health as Nature every 2 s for 20 s |
| Storm Chaser (buff) | Very resistant to Siege damage, and your melee hits apply 2% Rend (stacks to 25). From the Nephilim's sword |
| Shield Breaker (buff) | Bonus shield stamina damage. This is the lights reward |
| Shielded | The worm is immune to damage until the shield is broken |

## Rewards

As of Season 9, drops are 700-710 Gear Score items.

| Box | Contents |
|---|---|
| Major Sandworm Spoils (weekly) | Dark Matter, 500 Sandwurm Materia, **Minor Heartrune of The Devourer** (guaranteed), Gypsum Orbs, and up to 2 raid-only named items, with a higher chance of raid loot |
| Minor Sandworm Spoils (daily) | Dark Matter, Sandwurm Materia, Gypsum Orbs, and up to 1 raid-only named item |
| Notable | **Sclerite Pincer** (Great Axe). **Silken Cocoon** (light chest, GS 700-710), a raid-only named drop. **Tempest Fury** artifact: kill the worm with it equipped to unlock its perk |

Raid-only named items can be upgraded to 725 Gear Score, and some carry perk combinations you can't get elsewhere.

## Sources
- [Icy Veins: Sandwurm Elite Trial walkthrough](https://www.icy-veins.com/new-world/sandwurm-elite-trial-walkthrough)
- [New World: Elite Trial, Arena of Shah Neshen](https://www.newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/elite-trial-arena-of-shah-neshen-the-devourer)
- Route, attacks, phases, rotations, roles, shotcalling, preparation and rewards: raid guide videos and written raid guides, checked against in-game screenshots
- Debuffs, reward limits and the worm's stats: `StatusEffects*.csv`, `LootLimits.csv` and `VitalsBaseData` from the game data export

Back to [[1 Raids]] · [[New World Home]]

overrides/1-raids.body:
# 1 Raids

The three big group fights in Season 10: two 10-player raids and the 20-player Sandworm trial.

Related: [[1 Expeditions]] · [[1 Game Data]] · [[Set Pieces]] · [[Drop Limits]] · [[Consumables]] · [[1 Bosses]]

| Raid | Players | Where | Level / GS to aim for | Bosses | Main rewards |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[Isle of Night]] | 10 (opens with 6) | South coast of Nighthaven | 70 · 740–800 | Twin Jesters, Dahut and the Palatine Guards, Commander Thorpe | Spectral Wrath, Dreadwarden's and Hallowed Aegis set pieces (726–800 GS) |
| [[Hive of Gorgons]] | 10 (opens with 6) | South-east Cutlass Keys | 65 · 675+ | Echidna, Typhon, Broodmother Medusa | Gorgon's gear, Hoplite named items, artifacts (Azoth Conductors, Trsna, Elemental Band) |
| [[Sandworm]] | 20 (opens with 12) | Brimstone Sands (Elite Trial) | 65 · 690+ | Shah Neshen, the Devourer | Daily and weekly Sandworm Spoils, Sclerite Pincer, Heartrune of the Devourer |

## Checklist for every role

| Who | What to bring or do |
|---|---|
| Everyone | Ward potion and coating for the enemy type: Angry Earth for Hive, Lost for Isle of Night, Beast for Sandworm (all from the game data). See [[Consumables]] |
| Everyone | Attribute food for your main stat and a recovery food. The calculator's Target buttons show each boss's weaknesses |
| Tank | Hold the boss where the group can hit it; every fight has a "lead it away" step. Dreadwarden's is the Isle of Night tank set |
| Damage | Raid bosses resist Rend: it works at half strength. Bring the weakness damage type where you can (Fire/Slash for Hive, Nature/Strike for Isle of Night) |
| Healer | Assign who watches the tank and who watches the group; Hallowed Aegis is the Isle of Night healer set |

Gear for each role: [[Gear Basics]] · set pieces: [[Set Pieces]]

Back to [[New World Home]]

overrides/hive-of-gorgons.body:
# Hive of Gorgons

The first 10-player raid, in Cutlass Keys. It has three bosses with traps and Angry Earth mobs in between. This page follows the raid in the order you meet it.

Related: [[1 Raids]] · [[Consumables]] · [[Gems]] · [[Artifacts]] · [[Gear Basics]] · [[Status Effects]] · [[Trophies]]

## Getting in

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Players | 10 (opens with 6) |
| Level | 65 |
| Gear score | 675 minimum, ideally closer to 690. Getting to 725 takes a few clears of the raid |
| Entrance | South-east corner of Cutlass Keys, or the Activities tab |
| Start | You start in a safe zone, so sort roles and buffs there. The raid begins when someone crosses the main barrier after talking to Perseus |
| Run time | 25-45 minutes with a clean group; 60-120 minutes with a lot of wipes |
| Faction quests | Pick up 3 faction quests from the Cutlass Keys Faction Vendor first. Progress counts only on a full clear |
| Enemy type | Angry Earth. Angry Earth enemies are weak to Slash and Fire, so both are favoured (exact boss values under Preparation) |
| Bring | **Infused Angry Earth Ward Potion** · **Infused Angry Earth Coating** · **Major Angry Earth Combat Trophy** |
| Loot | Boss loot drops once per boss per week. Charms still drop after that |
| Weekly completion rewards | 1000 gold, 10,000 faction tokens, 500 azoth, 1 extra Gorgon Eye, 1 Azoth Conductor, 3 Chromatic Seals, 10 Gorgon Tokens, and a chance at a Gorgonite Schematic for GS 725 items with 1 locked perk and no crafting level needed |
| First-clear quest | Available in Cutlass Keys for your first clear: collect 3 items inside the raid. The reward is a Coconut and 2000 Doubloons |

## Preparation

Protection and gems change with each encounter. Swap them on the way.

| Encounter | Amulet | Gems |
|---|---|---|
| Trash between bosses | Thrust Protection | Full Onyx |
| Echidna | Strike Protection | Full Onyx |
| Typhon | Slash Protection | Full Onyx |
| Broodmother Medusa | Nature Protection | Amber, aiming for 40% Nature Protection |

**Boss stats (game data)**

All three bosses share these values.

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Family | Angry Earth |
| Boss health | 3.6× a standard raid enemy |
| Mitigation | 50% physical, 50% elemental, max 90% |
| Weak to | Fire (+5%), Slash (+2.5%) and Thrust (+1%) |
| Rend | Works at half strength: 50% boss resistance, 140% effective cap |
| Weaken | Works at about a third: 66% boss resistance, 147% effective cap |
| Damage over time | 10% resistance |

## Suggested group

Two groups of five.

| Group 1 | Group 2 |
|---|---|
| Tank | Flail |
| Healer  | SnS  |
| Rendbot  | Mage - Blunderbuss |
| Spear | Bleed Rapier |
| Evade | Evade  |

> [!tip] Against Broodmother Medusa, groups often switch to ranged builds: Bow and Musket. A ranged approach is far safer on first clears.

## 1. The way in

### Early trash

You run into boars, rats, corvids and spiders. Some packs have named variants with the same attack patterns, but tankier and hitting harder. Clearing these unlocks the path. Gatherables such as water motes and orichalcum nodes show up, but they are cosmetic and have no effect on the raid.

### Temple spawn area

At the temple you fight two named mobs, a boar and a corvid, supported by 2 normal corvids, 2 spiders and another boar. After they die a third named mob, a reindeer, spawns with a boar and a corvid on each side. Clear this set to unlock the puzzle room.

### Orb puzzle

A locked door has red orbs on each side and two pressure plates behind you. Pressing one plate spawns 2 spiders on that side and rotates that side's orbs. Pressing both plates together rotates all the orbs, but only one orb can be targeted at a time. Spiders keep spawning as long as someone stands on the plates, so let the tank hold aggro while the rest work the orbs. Shoot every orb until they all turn green: the door opens and the spiders despawn.

## 2. Echidna

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| Arena | Big and vertical. Pillars rise during the fight |
| Pillars | Ranged DPS stand on top. Higher up means bonus damage and stamina damage, and less of her rock armour |
| Tank | Kite her around the outer rim |
| Obsidian Crystals | Claw-like crystals come out of the ground. DPS kill them at once. Missing the second wave can wipe the raid |
| Crystal launch | A crystal landing on you while you're on a pillar kills you. Dodge or jump off |
| Stamina break | When her stamina breaks she flips over. Everyone goes melee, applies rend and hits the upper middle of her body |
| Resistance | She deals mostly Strike damage: Onyx gems in armour. Strike Protection is the main protection to run, Slash Protection second |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Effect |
|---|---|
| Obsidian Weakness | Take 40% more damage while near an Obsidian Crystal |
| Rooted | Rooted until the Obsidian Missile is destroyed (up to 10 s) |
| Threat Detected (3 levels) | The lower you stand, the more of her rock armour soaks your hits |
| In the Clear | Bonus damage and stamina damage from pillar height |
| She's Exposed! | Bonus damage hitting her back after a stagger |

### The fight

Echidna is the first boss. The fight has a lot of Strike-damage mechanics, with a wipe mechanic every few rotations. As soon as you pass the puzzle door you enter a large arena; Echidna leaps down and the way behind you seals.

### Attacks

| Attack | What happens |
|---|---|
| Ground Slam (opening) | She opens with a ground slam, and the damage lands slightly before her hand touches down. Dodge early, or block to reduce it |
| Stone Rubble into Pillars | Rubble spawns, then seconds later white stone pillars rise. Standing on rubble launches you onto the pillar and damages you. She destroys pillars if she is lured into them. Pillars come short, medium and tall; mining a tall one makes it shorter so you can climb it |
| Rock Projectiles | She roars and raises her tail, rocks form around her, then she slams the tail down and launches them across the arena. They deal Strike damage and must be dodged: blocking still takes damage. There is usually a safe zone where the rocks first spawned. Standing right behind her can be as deadly as the rocks |
| Tail Swipe | A wide sweep of her tail. It cannot be dodged, so block it. Staying at her sides rather than right behind her makes it less likely to hit you |
| Claw Swipes | Mostly aimed at the tank but can hit nearby players. They often chain into a Head Stomp, which deals heavy stamina damage: dodge or grit through it |
| Head Stomp | She slams her head into the ground and sends a shockwave across the arena that damages everyone |
| Claw Stomp and Claw Scrape | Claw Stomp slams both hands forward and scrapes the ground. Claw Scrape strikes to one side, then scrapes across the ground. Either hand can be used, and both deal heavy melee damage in their path |
| Melee Bite | A close-range lunge at the tank. Two versions: an immediate lunge, and one with a slight delay that baits dodges |

### Mechanics in detail

**Pillar height.** Your height decides your damage. Despite the tall-pillar buff, melee DPS on the ground is more efficient overall.

| Height | Effect |
|---|---|
| Ground | Threat Detected: -70% damage |
| Low pillar | Threat Still Detected: -60% damage |
| Mid pillar | Threat Barely Detected: -40% damage |
| Tall pillar | In the Clear: +10% damage and +300% stamina damage |

**Obsidian Crystals and spikes.** After some ground slams she launches Obsidian spikes across the arena. Standing near one applies Obsidian Weakness: 40% more damage taken from everything. Destroy them quickly. A spike that lands on a pillar makes the pillar glow white and then explode, dealing heavy damage to anyone touching it; the spike is destroyed with it, so glowing pillars need no cleanup. If spikes are left, her tremors can trigger a Thrust attack: vines with purple effects erupt from the crystals and heavily damage nearby players.

**Stamina break: the biggest damage window.** She has a stamina bar under her health for the whole fight. When it empties she collapses onto her side, often the side away from most players, and exposes her back as the weak point. Everyone moves to her exposed side at once and bursts with everything. During the collapse, melee players get She's Exposed: +200% Empower, unclamped. It can happen several times in the fight. Call it out when the stamina bar is close to breaking.

### Phases

**Wipe mechanic at 50% health.** She moves to the centre of the arena and ground-slams. Every pillar glows white and explodes, killing anyone standing on one. Any Obsidian spikes still standing also detonate, and a single spike left can wipe the raid. Survivors still take a damage-over-time effect, so go into this phase with the arena cleared. During the animation no spikes or pillars spawn, so it is a free damage window: stack on her and use everything.

> [!warning] Always destroy the spikes before pushing her past 50%.

**Phase two: Pounce.** One random player gets a white marker over their head. She rears back and leaps across the arena at them; the landing deals massive Strike damage, and the tremor damages everyone in the arena. She does this 3-4 times in a row, and the last pounce always targets the tank or whoever holds aggro. The marked player dodges at the last moment. Blocking reduces the damage but still takes some and drains stamina fast. She can pounce players on pillars too, and a direct landing deals full damage.

**Upgraded attacks in phase two.** Rock Projectiles no longer have a safe zone, so everyone must time their dodges. Claw Scrape now launches rocks as it scrapes.

**Rotation changes.** After a few attacks she gets ready for another wipe and summons spikes again. This time she does not pounce straight away: destroy the spikes first, then get ready. From here on, Pounce comes at the end of each rotation instead of the start.

## 3. Corridor and lake

### Narrow corridor after Echidna

Once Echidna is defeated, the path opens to a narrow corridor. On entry one of each enemy type spawns, with the wolf as the named elite. Clear them and head upstairs to more mobs; the door will not open until every enemy is cleared. Journal Page 1 of 3 is hidden in the corner here.

### Lake area

After the checkpoint a massive door opens into a large outdoor zone. There is a named wolf on the left, a named boar across the lake, a named reindeer near the far stairs, and two wolves plus a named wolf in the far distance, with spiders, rats, a reindeer, a corvid and other enemies scattered around. All of it is optional, and you can run past to the next door. To go on you only need to defeat the named boar and the corvid near him. Once they are down the gate at the top of the stairs opens, and skipped enemies will not follow you past it. Journal Page 2 is next to the rat by the pool.

## 4. Medusa's Maze

The path leads back to Perseus. Speak to him to open the next door and enter Medusa's Maze. Inside is a statue of Medusa above three unlit orbs; the goal is to turn all three green at the same time. Killing the spiders unlocks the platforms, and it takes two players standing on them to activate one orb. All six platforms across the maze must be pressed at the same time to open the gate.

> [!warning] Two roaming Medusas patrol the maze. They cannot be killed. Their attacks include a lethal line-of-sight gaze beam and a rushing claw strike. Use walls and corners to break line of sight.

Most groups assign one or two players to kite the Medusas while the others clear spiders and get the platforms ready. The central square room is a reliable kiting spot. Once all the platforms are active the gate opens, and the Medusa clones cannot follow you through the door.

## 5. Typhon

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| DPS check | Three phases. Each adds mobs and removes pillars. If the pillars run out before the next phase, you wipe |
| Weapons | Melee is fine here: spear, rapier or hatchet |
| Thorn lane | The left, middle or right lane glows red. Move out before the thorns come up |
| Targeted thorns | Red icon over your head: run to the edge away from the group and keep moving. More players get marked as his HP drops |
| Iron Maiden | Thorn cages trap players and hurt over time. Break them fast |
| Insta-charge | Instant kill. Hide behind a pillar |
| Corvids | Kill them fast or Typhon eats them for buffs. Gravity Well and Shockwave group them. Scorpion's Sting pulls them out of vines |
| Resistance | Slash Protection amulet, Thrust Protection second, full Onyx gems. His attacks mix Slash, Thrust, Strike and Nature, with Slash the most common |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Effect |
|---|---|
| Blighted Blood | Bleed 2% base health per second and take 15% more damage, 15 s |
| Painful Confinement | Thorn cage: 5% base Nature damage every 0.5 s, up to 12 s |
| Thorn Shackles | "Unless you found some cover, Typhon will execute you." 6 s. This is the charge: get behind a pillar |

### The fight

Typhon is the second boss and a true DPS check. The faster your group deals damage, the shorter and safer the fight; a group short on damage or coordination gets a long fight that punishes hard. A balanced group with Rend, Weaken and Empower controls the flow of the fight.

As you approach, the entrance seals and the arena splits into three sections for a three-phase fight. Typhon is very mobile, often turning or leaping, so the tank must hold aggro and keep him facing away from the group. Everyone else stays behind him, ready to move. Most of his basic attacks are claw swipes to his front, so behind him is generally safe, but his mobility means you are never fully out of danger.

> [!warning] Every attack applies a bleed that cannot be dispelled, even on a block, so dodging is the safest answer. He pauses slightly between moves, which gives you chances to recover stamina.

### Attacks

| Attack | What happens |
|---|---|
| Arena Vines | He howls and vines grow at the edges of the arena. Red warning lines then cross the floor, and where they meet, that section erupts in Nature and Thrust spikes. It can be the left, right or centre section at random, so the tank lures him away from the active one |
| Grasping Thorns | He leaps backwards and slams the ground, sending vines crawling forward in a straight line. They trap players on contact and hold them in place with damaging spikes. Destroy the vines to free yourself or a teammate |
| Red Circles | A circle vine attack that ticks several times, each tick erupting vines from the ground. If you're targeted, move away from your teammates at once. A straight-line sprint is usually enough; don't panic-dodge, because with grey stamina you'll be too slow to escape the tick |
| Scent of Blood | He jumps and slams the ground in front of him, damaging anyone in a rectangle and spawning spikes. Watch for the wind-up and dodge before impact |
| Bite | Hits anyone in front of him, with a short wind-up that gives time to dodge. It also applies a bleed |
| Ground Slam Wave | He runs to the centre, jumps and lands with a shockwave that sends out four circular waves of rocks dealing Strike damage. Dodge them, or block if you must |
| Swipe Attack | Aimed at the tank but hits everyone nearby. Especially dangerous when he has Howl stacks, which give him 30% lifesteal per stack on this attack |

### Mechanics in detail

**Adds and absorption buffs.** Typhon summons spiders, one corvid and one wolf. Clear them quickly: after a short delay he absorbs any adds still alive and gains strong buffs.

| Add | If absorbed |
|---|---|
| Corvid | Empower: +30% damage per stack, up to 10 stacks |
| Wolf | Howl: Nature damage over time on every player, based on a percentage of their max health and rising with each stack |
| Spider | Less of a threat, but slows and damages players |

Always kill the corvids first: they are harder to pin down and give the most dangerous buff.

**Sniffing for Blood (the charge).** After absorbing adds he moves to the centre, picks a random player and marks them with a large black eye icon. A few seconds later that player is stunned and he leaps at them for a finishing blow. If it lands, it is instant death for them and anyone nearby. The marked player must hide behind one of the four pillars before the stun. He crashes into the pillar instead and is briefly stunned, which gives the team a safe damage window. The pillar is destroyed afterwards. With good damage, your group can reach 70% health using one pillar, or none.

### Phases

| Phase | Health | Pillars | Red Circles targets | Adds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 100% to 70% | 4 | 2 players | Spiders, 1 corvid, 1 wolf |
| 2 | 70% to 30% | 3 | 3 players | 1 corvid, 1 wolf and a third of either kind |
| 3 | 30% to 0% | 2 | 4 players | 2 corvids, 2 wolves |

**Phase changes.** At 70% he becomes invincible, howls and knocks every player back. Any adds still alive die without being absorbed. Blocking can stop the knockback, but it cannot be dodged. The way forward opens as he moves to the next section. The same happens at 30%. Attack patterns stay similar, with new threats each phase. Kill the corvids first, then the wolves, so the buffs don't stack on him. In the last phase he uses everything he has: ideally your damage finishes him before the pillars run out and you start losing players one by one.

## 6. Road to Medusa

With Typhon defeated the path splits into two routes, both uphill through trash you can clear or skip. A common trick is to pull enemies back into the boss arena, where they die automatically.

Medusa statues appear here: rotating heads that scan the area and use Medusa's gaze when they see you. The gaze petrifies you and deals continuous damage that kills you without healing. Move behind the statues and stay out of their line of sight.

Two new enemy types arrive: gorillas, which roll across the area and smash into players, and elephants, with heavy AoE attacks and knockbacks. Elephants are especially dangerous and should always be killed first. Continue uphill to a named wolf, more trash and another elephant, with a Medusa statue overlooking them. Pull enemies downhill, out of the statue's range, and fight them there.

### Mushroom poison and cleansing fountains

Ahead is a gate covered in thick vines. Standing inside them builds up Nature and applies a poison debuff that spreads to nearby teammates. The same mechanic returns in the final boss fight, so learn it here.

Nearby is a fountain of blue cleansing water. Interacting with it gives you a ball of cleansing energy to throw on the ground, which makes a small cleansing circle that removes poison and build-up. Use it to clear the vines and cleanse your group.

At the fork the left path is a dead end, so go right. It has two more Medusa statues and packs of corvids and spiders, which you can snipe from below to lure them down, or push through and fight together. At the top are a named boar, another elephant and several gorillas.

### Mushroom arena

A circular arena full of poisonous mushrooms, surrounded by fountains. Once you step inside, the entrance closes and you must use the fountains to manage the poison while fighting waves.

| Wave | Enemies |
|---|---|
| 1 | A named corvid, an elephant and supporting mobs |
| 2 | A named wolf, a reindeer and a boar |

To go on you must cleanse the arena fully and clear the vines from both gates. Each fountain has a cooldown, so coordinate.

> [!tip] Use the cleansing fountain behind you before the fight starts to pre-cleanse the arena and unlock the fountains early.

### Split path

Split into two groups of five. At the start of each path are sealed gates with platforms, and three players must stand on the platforms at the same time to open both gates. Each path has levers and gates linked to the other side: pulling a lever on one path opens a gate for the other group, so progress needs constant cooperation.

| Path | What's on it |
|---|---|
| Left | Starts with two spiders and needs the right side to pull levers. Inside are more spiders, a corvid and a wolf. Journal Page 3 is on this path, near the corvid |
| Right | Starts by pulling a lever that opens the first gate for the left side. Then spiders, a boar, a corvid, rats and vines, and later a wolf, a gorilla and several Medusa statues |

When both groups finish their routes and pull the twin levers, the gate opens onto the final arena.

## 7. Broodmother Medusa

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| Difficulty | Easier than Typhon, with no DPS check |
| Eggs and flowers | Ranged DPS destroy them as they appear. Eggs that hatch spawn random mobs |
| Sleep powder | White powder puts you to sleep for up to 60 seconds, taking 5% base Nature damage per second, unless someone cleanses you |
| Cleansing | Grab the glowing ball from a fountain on the outer rim and throw it to cleanse an area |
| Tank cleanser | One player keeps the tank's debuffs and DoTs down |
| Screech and charge | After a cleanse she screeches, picks a player and charges. Dodge it |
| Good DPS picks | Fire Staff, or Hatchet (it can be thrown, and Berserk helps you survive) |
| Resistance | Nature Protection amulet and Amber gems, aiming for at least 40% Nature Protection |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Effect |
|---|---|
| Envenomed | 2.5% health per tick, 5 s |
| Medusa's Poison (pool) | 3% health per tick, 5 s |
| Gorgon's Gaze | 15% slow for 15 s |
| Petrifying | 50% of health and 50% slow over 8 s. Don't get caught by the gaze twice |

### The fight

Medusa is the final boss. Once the two levers are pulled the central gate opens. The fight has heavy Nature damage, constant cleansing, and needs good coordination to handle eggs, flowers and her deadly charges. For first clears a ranged approach is recommended: the fight is far safer from a distance until you know it.

At the start a large flower hangs from the ceiling: that is Medusa, curled up and waiting. The four corners of the arena have cleansing fountains, which you need for the mushroom infection throughout the fight.

### Mechanics in detail

**Ceiling Flowers.** Three hanging flowers start dormant but bloom several times. When they bloom they get their own health bars and use one of two attacks:

| Flower attack | What happens |
|---|---|
| Barbs | Three projectiles land and leave barbs on the floor. Touching a barb applies a fast-ticking bleed |
| Sleep Smoke | White smoke lingers in the arena. Stay in it and you fall asleep, taking 5% base Nature damage per second for up to 60 seconds. The counter is a cleanse splash from a fountain, so be ready to react when a teammate is caught |

**Ooze puddles and mushroom infection.** She keeps spawning ooze puddles under and around herself as she moves and attacks. Standing in one adds infection stacks, each dealing 0.5% base Nature damage per second. At ten stacks the infection becomes active: a poison circle debuff that damages you and can spread to nearby teammates. Cleansing is a constant job, and most groups give one player the fountain splashes to clear infection before it gets dangerous.

> [!warning] Never throw a cleanse at Medusa herself. If one hits her she charges forward, leaving an ooze trail and dealing lethal damage.

**Eggs.** Every few attacks she turns and vomits three large eggs into the arena. Eggs spawn at 50% health and regenerate until they hatch. At full health they hatch into a random raid mob: rats, spiders, corvids, reindeer, boars, wolves, elephants or gorillas. Eggs are very tanky but take +70% damage from Slash and Strike, so greatswords and hatchets are ideal. Some eggs hatch on impact; others land unhatched and give a short window to break them. Either put 1-2 players with the right weapons on egg duty, which is safer, or let them hatch and deal with the mobs, which is riskier.

**In short.** Cleanse regularly and keep infection stacks off. Break eggs fast with Slash and Strike weapons. Kill ceiling flowers as soon as they bloom. Stay out of the white smoke. Handle the charges safely.

### Attacks

| Attack | What happens |
|---|---|
| Landing Slam | As you near the centre she uncoils and drops to the floor. The landing is not just an animation: it kills you if she lands on you |
| Hair Toss | A basic frontal attack aimed mainly at the tank. Stay at her sides or behind her |
| Wide Hand Slashes | Wide frontal swipes that punish anyone in front of her. The tank holds position; everyone else stays off her front |
| Triple Stomp | A three-hit frontal sequence. Don't stand in front of her during it |
| Back Flower | At times a flower blooms on her back with its own health bar. It launches barbs into the arena until it is destroyed |
| Tail Attack | She glances behind her, then slams her tail left and right, damaging and staggering anyone behind her |
| Vine Pull | Pulls players in, dealing damage and a short stun. Be ready to reposition quickly |
| Infecting Stomp | She turns and stomps both hands into the ground, sending mushrooms across the arena and giving active mushroom infection to a random player. Cleanse that player at once, and everyone stays out of the slam area |

### Phase change at 40% health

At 40% she blocks every fountain and adds a charge like the cleanse-triggered one: she turns and rushes in a random direction, leaving an ooze trail, and keeps using it for the rest of the fight. Don't hit her with a cleanse in this phase, as it triggers an extra charge. To get cleansing back, damage the blocked fountains until they clear. From then on, one random fountain blocks from time to time and must be damaged again before you can use it.

## Loot

| Drop | From |
|---|---|
| Azoth Conductors (medium pants artifact) | Echidna |
| Trsna (War Hammer artifact) | Typhon |
| Elemental Band (ring artifact) | Medusa |
| Gorgon's weapons (every weapon and shield type), Hoplite Flail | Medusa |
| Gorgonite Inductor, Gorgon's Eye, Chromatic Seal | Crafting/upgrade materials |
| Hive of Gorgons Tokens | Currency for the raid vendor |

> [!info] The three artifacts are not tied to the weekly loot cap and can be farmed. Each is guaranteed on the 5th kill of its boss.

### Per boss

Everything below except the artifacts counts towards the weekly raid loot cap.

| Boss | Drops |
|---|---|
| Echidna | She drops loot near the arena entrance. One named hoplite jewellery piece (upgradable); one non-named jewellery piece with fixed stats; 1 Gorgon Eye (guaranteed); 10 Damaged Gorgon Eyes if you're under the weekly cap; Azoth Conductors |
| Typhon | Loot drops where he falls. One named hoplite gear piece (upgradable, loot-biased to the armour weight you have equipped); random Gorgon gear up to GS 725, loot-biased; 1 Gorgon Eye (guaranteed); 10 Damaged Gorgon Eyes if you're under the weekly cap; Trsna |
| Broodmother Medusa | One named hoplite weapon (upgradable, loot-biased, usually with Distained Infliction and Keenly Jagged); a non-named Gorgon weapon up to GS 725, loot-biased to the weapons you have equipped; 2 Gorgon Eyes (guaranteed); 20 Damaged Gorgon Eyes (guaranteed); Elemental Band |

## Sources
- [Icy Veins: Hive of Gorgons walkthrough](https://www.icy-veins.com/new-world/hive-of-gorgons-raid-walkthrough)
- [StudioLoot: Hive of Gorgons guide](https://www.studioloot.com/new-world/articles/complete-hive-of-gorgons-guide)
- [New World: Hive of Gorgons deep dive](https://newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/the-hive-of-the-gorgons-raid-deep-dive)
- Route, boss attacks, phases and per-boss loot: raid guide videos, checked against in-game screenshots
- Boss stats and attack names: the game's creature data and boss animation files
- Debuffs: `StatusEffects_AI*.csv` from the game data export

# Isle of Night

Season 10's 10-player raid, off the coast of Nighthaven. It has three bosses and is the only source of the Spectral Wrath, Dreadwarden's and Hallowed Aegis set pieces. This page follows the raid in the order you meet it.

Related: [[1 Raids]] · [[Set Pieces]] · [[Gear Sets]] · [[Drop Limits]] · [[Gear Basics]] · [[Gems]] · [[Status Effects]]

> [!info] The strategy here comes from raid guides and in-game runs. The debuff tables and enemy stats come straight from the game files.

## Getting in

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Players | 10 (you can open it with 6 to practise) |
| Level | 70 |
| Gear score | Guides say aim for 780–800. One lists 650+ as the bare minimum |
| Unlock | Finish the Nighthaven story quests and the Season 10 intro missions |
| Entrance | Skull icon on Nighthaven's south coast. Nearest fast travel: Church of Grivaros. Or queue through Group Finder (Raids) |
| Loot | One guide says there's no weekly loot cap. Not confirmed |
| Enemy type |  **Infused Lost Ward Potion** · **Infused Lost Coating** · **Major Lost Combat Trophy**. Lost enemies are weak to Nature, Strike and Ice (exact values under Preparation) |
| Dying and wiping | The puzzles between bosses have no penalty for dying or wiping |

## Preparation

Gems and amulets change per boss, because each boss hits with a different damage type.

| Encounter | Gems and amulet |
|---|---|
| Twin Jesters | Everyone: full **Jasper** (Strike protection). Nearly all the damage is Strike |
| Dahut: DPS and healers | Slash protection amulet and **Moonstone**. DPS can add about two Arcane gems to survive the totem and sword hits |
| Dahut: off tank | **Onyx** plus a Slash protection amulet. Dahut deals mostly Slash, and only the off tank needs Slash protection |
| Dahut: main tank | **Onyx**, plus an amulet against whatever hurts most while holding three guards |
| Thorpe: everyone | **Sapphire** (Arcane), because of his arcane pools and volcanoes |
| Thorpe: lightbearers | **Moonstone** with 2–3 **Sapphire**, and keep Slash protection: the light damage is Standard damage, which Slash protection covers |

**Boss stats (game data)**

| Boss | Health |
|---|---|
| Twin Jesters | 7.5× a standard raid enemy |
| Dahut | 3× a standard raid enemy |
| Thorpe | 10.5× a standard raid enemy |

All three bosses are Lost, with 50% physical and 50% elemental mitigation (max 90%). Rend works at half strength (50% resilience), Weaken at about a third (66%), and damage over time at 90% (10%). They're slightly weak to Nature (+5%), Strike (+2.5%) and Ice (+1.5%).

## Suggested group

| Group 1 | Group 2 |
|---|---|
| Main tank | Off tank |
| Main healer | Off healer |
| Spear DPS | Evade Rapier |
| Buff bot | Evade Rapier |
| Blood Rapier | Flex |

> [!info] Thorpe needs no off tank: one main tank and two healers. Everyone except the main tank should carry a ranged second weapon for his ghosts.

## 1. Twin Jesters

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| Overlapping AoEs and traps | Two bosses in one fight. Don't stand where both can hit you |
| Copies ("Find the real Jester") | The Jesters spawn three decoys and everyone gets +40% move speed for 25 s. Spread out and find the real one, stagger it, then everybody DPS |
| Add waves | Carcasses, woodcutters, villagers and a cryptkeeper join in. Tank picks them up |
| Trap levers (blue glow) | Two trappers, one on each lever (left and right). Pulling it slows the adds and damages them |
| Rewarding Audience | Players near the Jesters buff their attack and damage absorption. Only stand close if you need to |
| Positioning | No split needed. Stack near the tank so heals and cleaves land |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Effect |
|---|---|
| Pranked | 20% slow, take 20% more damage, deal 20% less damage, for 12 s |
| Burn (Hellring, Fiery Cackle trail, hits) | Fire damage over time, 1–5 s |
| Slow | 30% move speed reduction (3 s after explosions) |

### Roles for this fight

| Role | Job |
|---|---|
| Trappers (2) | Ideally two Evade players with an **Ice Gauntlet** second weapon, one per lever. They leave DPS to set **Ice Shower** traps near the tree edge, so the adds can't path around them and die at once |
| Shooter (1+) | Anyone: a flex or shield DPS, an extra Evade, even the healer. Grabs ballista bolts and fires the ballista in the stagger phase |
| Healer | Needed for **Void Blade** |

### Damage windows

When the boss drops, go to his back, the purple side, not the white: almost every hit crits from behind. His back slam can be blocked, Flurried through or dodged. Break the barrels.

Early on, adds spawn, and he can consume them to heal, up to almost half his health. Enough DPS brings it back; speedrun groups kill the early adds at once.

### Adds, trappers and the ballista

- If adds spawn on one side, they're spawning on both.
- The trap kills most adds, but not Brutes: warn the group and dodge them.
- Killing certain adds spawns a ballista bolt. Grab it and preload a ballista, often one of the Ice Gauntlet trappers. Every ballista starts loaded but can't be reloaded after firing. Fire it during the stagger phase.
- Let the woodcutters go: kill the ghouls and carcasses; the axemen matter less. A woodcutter on the way means all the other adds are coming, so leave early.
- The left side spawns Nagas, which hit hard. The left trapper needs another DPS to help.

### Mechanics in detail

**The real Jester.** He spawns three clones. The real one still shows your DoTs (bleeds, burns, poison, rupture), and stands tall pointing while the three clones crouch with their hands pointing. A wrong guess hits every player with an explosion: about 6,350 damage the first time, 9,000+ the second, and later a one-shot.

**"Can you think outside the box?"** He throws boxes on the ground. Stepping inside a box's circle sets it off, with a stagger and decent damage. A ranged player shoots the ones near the group so nobody triggers them; they pop up after a while.

**"Who's the lucky winner?"** He teleports to a ranged player. Hold block when he teleports in case he jumps on you, then go back to traps and DPS. A hex mechanic gives time to leave or get some damage in.

**Final 10%.** At the last health bar he phases, and any adds near him heal him (no adds, no heal). You have about 35 seconds to DPS; high damage can take a bar in about 10 seconds. If adds spawn, the main tank taunts them all and pulls them away so the DPS don't get staggered.

## 2. Dahut and the Palatine Guards

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| Four guards | Archer, Shieldbearer, Swordsman and Halberdier |
| Tanking | The main tank holds three guards; the off tank takes the Archer |
| 50% stasis | A guard goes inactive at 50% HP. Once all four are at 50% they come back. Then kill them one at a time |
| Dahut | Appears after the last guard. She's fast and drops fire and abyss areas on the floor |
| Guards return | In Dahut's phase the guards revive and the raid handles them again. Once they're down, everyone joins the off tank on Dahut; the main tank only holds the Archer |
| Abyss mark | Marked players are targeted by her Dance of Death. They counter "Abyss Instability", so marked players go to the guards |
| "Regroup with your allies!" | Stack up to share the damage |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Palatine Rend | Swordsman | Take 10% more damage for 5 s |
| Disease | Shieldbearer (gong) | 50% less healing taken for 3 s |
| Decimate Jail | Halberdier | 2 s stun, then 5 s with no stamina regen |
| Palatine Smite | Halberdier | 30% slow for 2 s |
| Stranded Tether | Archer | Rooted for 2 s |
| Blazing Fission | Archer (ground) | 1% Fire damage per second per stack, 10 s |
| Standing in the abyss | Dahut | 30% slow and 83% less stamina regen while you stand in it |
| Abyssal Drain | Dahut (Purging Blade) | No stamina regen |

> [!tip] Tank note: the Halberdier's jail takes away your stamina regen. Don't be blocking on low stamina when it lands.

> [!tip] This fight isn't timed. Take your time; rushing as a learner makes it harder.

### The guards

| Guard | What to do |
|---|---|
| Archer | When she reaches the H or C marker she runs to the middle and casts Rain of Fire: run away. The off tank needs open space and shouldn't run into the fire to DPS. Reign of Flame arrows: run away from the centre and come back when the fire is gone |
| Shieldbearer | Charges the player with the shield icon, usually the furthest away. The off tank tries to be furthest; everyone else keeps within the off tank's radius so the target is already next to them. Wait until he turns and walks back to the main tank before taunting, or he ignores the taunt. Break his stamina bar before he reaches the centre |
| Halberdier | Keep him on the outside. In the centre he pulls everybody in and slams, which is near-certain death; outside you're pulled but too far from the slam to die. His prison puts you to sleep for about 3 s: 300 DEX or **Berserk** frees you |
| Swordsman | The most dangerous: he gains an empower stack every time he hits, up to 10. Bring him to the centre first, where he detonates. Kill him first, since he moves the most, and stack the other two on top of him |

**Stacking the guards.** The main tank taunts every guard, the Archer included, so everyone (the off tank too) can hit the Archer's back. Aggro shows as the nameplate turning red. Line the guards up slightly behind a dead guard's feet, since they fall forward. The main tank gives **Beloved** and buffs.

**In-n-out rings.** Safe in the centre, then on the outer layer, then the centre again, then not the centre: go out, then back in. You can i-frame through, but learners should do the mechanic.

### Instability phase

The torches turn purple and players get spiked crowns: the Instability damage buff. The guards glow and will explode, but take massive damage, and you have only 25 seconds to kill them. Don't burst the guards down beforehand: get them to about 10–15% health and finish them in this phase.

When the guards revive, kill them in the first revive round. On the second respawn, get them low again and kill them during Instability.

### Dahut's crown teleport

When Dahut turns into purple mist, she teleports to each player with a crown. Everyone scatters and uses a Grit Ward Potion. The first hit staggers: Grit or **Stoneform** prevents it, and the rest can be dodged. The tank can block her hits.

> [!warning] The last crown holder gets a soak mechanic and dies instantly unless at least 3–4 players soak with them. It can't be i-framed or riposted.

**Other mechanics.**
- Arcane swords form pillars. They can be killed; they slow you and grow over time.
- The main healer drops **Sacred Ground** and **Beacon** on the main tank, then helps with damage.
- The main tank stays at the edge. If the main tank taunted Dahut earlier, a later taunt does nothing: the off tank heavy-attacks to take aggro. Keep her at the edge because of the hex.
- After the second respawn only eight players are on the boss. Two players out lowers the damage, but fewer adds make the Instability phase easier.
- **Defy Death** procs even if an add kills you, which puts it on a one-minute timer.
- An off tank on Sword and Shield can swap to a **Greatsword** to break the Shieldbearer's stamina faster, and to a **Hatchet** for Divine Death and **Berserk**, an instant Grit outside the grip ward pods.

## 3. Commander Thorpe

The final boss, called Overlord Thorpe in the game data. Two lightbearers take turns carrying a golden orb while the rest of the raid deals damage, and everyone deals with the six ghosts.

| Debuff | Effect | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Spear Bearer | Holder keeps gaining Fragile Soul and pulls Thorpe's focus | The orb (relic) the lightbearers carry. Plan who takes it next and rotate it |
| Fragile Soul | 4% base Fire damage every 1.2 s for 15 s | The cost of carrying the relic. Healers watch the carrier |
| Rooted (lost the relic) | Rooted for 6 s after losing the relic | Don't drop it carelessly. When Thorpe steals the orb, the carrier takes heavy damage (10 stacks tick hard) and is rooted; guides give about 10 s |
| Mistlocked | Soul locked down: 3 s root | Impaling Mistlock: dodge the impale |
| Soul Exhaustion | Can't run or dodge for 4 s | Don't get caught near other hazards |
| Rend | Take 10% more damage for 20 s | Tank swap or a defensive cooldown if it stacks with other damage |

### Roles for this fight

| Role | Job |
|---|---|
| Main tank | The only tank. Holds Thorpe |
| Lightbearers (2) | One healer and one Evade Rapier with a ranged weapon (**Musket** or Bow). They take turns with the orb, and their main job is killing ghosts |
| Second healer | Stays with the group |
| Everyone else | DPS, with a ranged second weapon for the ghosts |

### The orb

- Standing where the sword spawns is dangerous because of the knockback. The lightbearers alternate: one stands in front of the boss to keep damaging while the orb comes. After intercepting the first orb you can keep damaging for a while before he steals it.
- After his first health bar, lightbearers shouldn't stand near Thorpe: he always goes to the furthest player.
- If Thorpe reaches the sword buff, he drops holy swords on everyone.
- If a lightbearer dies, the sword buff resets into the relic and the other lightbearer picks it up. A dead lightbearer can spectate and call mechanics.
- As DPS, when the steal comes towards you, roll back into it: it can skip you and go straight to him.
- There's a visual bug where the sword stays on your head after it has moved to the other player. You're still rooted.
- **Mortal Aggression** helps with healing.

### The ghosts

Six ghosts spawn at fixed corners. If Thorpe's shockwave hits a living ghost, it spawns a specific add: the Shieldbearer, the Jester, Dahut, the Archer, the Swordsman or the Halberdier. Ghosts can also spawn adds and cast crescent waves, and Thorpe buffs them over time.

- A ghost with four shards detonates. You survive if Thorpe's jump doesn't catch you, and you can i-frame the detonation. The lightbearers and ranged call out ghosts at 2–3 shards, and everyone kills any ghost they see.
- Kill ghosts when he shoots big grey souls at them, before the soul arrives or they detonate.
- In the shadow phase, give each player a ghost. Ghosts with their hands facing him are feeding him souls, which means a big buff or a detonation. Staggering Thorpe out of the shadow mechanic skips it.
- To stack ghosts, get them low rather than killing them straight away.

### Other mechanics

- Ring-around-the-rosy: a big, slow beam that's easy to avoid.
- When the Jester spawns, everyone jumps on him. His "Who's the lucky winner?" teleports to the furthest player, so be ready to block.
- In the last 20% of his health the mechanics stay the same but speed up: more adds, and ghosts gain shards faster.
- There's no DPS phase at the end: keep repeating the mechanics until he dies.
